ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with dark dorsal markings and a distinct white spot on the snout. It features a granular belly and lacks vomerine teeth. Family: Rhacophoridae. IUCN: Data Deficient.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes manipurensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow-to-orange groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs, which contrast sharply with its dorsal color.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes manipurensis* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and bamboo thickets in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes manipurensis* is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small invertebrates among the dense vegetation of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes manipurensis* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with clutches laid in vegetation or leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes manipurensis* is endemic to the hill ranges of Manipur, India, where it inhabits moist forest environments at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes manipurensis* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in forest habitats.
